text:
## Observations

1. With 1-based coordinates, a cell at row r and column c belongs to the square rotated in operation i exactly when i is at most its layer number, the minimum of r, c, N + 1 − r, and N + 1 − c.
2. A clockwise quarter-turn sends (r, c) to (c, N + 1 − r). It permutes the four distances used to compute the layer number, so a color stays on the same layer as it moves.
3. A color on layer d therefore moves in exactly d operations. Four quarter-turns return a cell to its starting position, and every quarter-turn is a bijection within its layer.

## Solution sketch

1. “With 1-based coordinates, a cell at row r and column c belongs to the square rotated in operation i exactly when i is at most its layer number, the minimum of r, c, N + 1 − r, and N + 1 − c.”

   Read the input grid, allocate a separate output grid, and visit each input cell once. Compute its layer number d from its original coordinates.

2. “A clockwise quarter-turn sends (r, c) to (c, N + 1 − r). It permutes the four distances used to compute the layer number, so a color stays on the same layer as it moves.”

   Track each input color using the same d throughout. Begin at its original coordinates and use the quarter-turn mapping to calculate its destination.

3. “A color on layer d therefore moves in exactly d operations. Four quarter-turns return a cell to its starting position, and every quarter-turn is a bijection within its layer.”

   Apply the mapping d modulo 4 times, then write the input color to the resulting output cell. The bijections ensure that every output cell is written exactly once. The same rule covers N = 2, where all cells turn once, and layers whose number is a multiple of four, where every color returns to its starting cell. Print the completed grid row by row. Each cell takes constant time, so the algorithm uses O(N²) time and O(N²) space for the grids.

isolation.mechanism: codex exec, fresh ephemeral session, empty temporary working directory, user config and exec rules ignored, read-only sandbox, web search and listed features disabled, credential-like variables removed from the environment
isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
